blocks.text: Linearly independent vectors
The vectors \(X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_n\) are linearly independent if
\[\alpha_1X_1+\alpha_2X_2+\cdots+\alpha_nX_n=0\]
implies \(\alpha_1=\alpha_2=\cdots=\alpha_n=0\). Otherwise, the vectors are linearly dependent.

pages.heading: Notebook p. 17 · Algebraic and geometric multiplicity

blocks.text: Algebraic multiplicity (AM)

If an eigenvalue \(\lambda\) occurs \(t\) times as a root of the characteristic equation, its algebraic multiplicity is \(t\). In the class note, AM is described as the number of repetitions of \(\lambda\).
Geometric multiplicity (GM)
The number of linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to an eigenvalue \(\lambda\) is called the geometric multiplicity of \(\lambda\).

Diagonalization of a matrix

If a matrix \(A\) is similar to a diagonal matrix \(D\), then \(A\) is said to be diagonalized, and \(D\) is called a diagonal form of \(A\). Thus, if \(A\) is diagonalizable, there exists a non-singular matrix \(P\) such that
Notes from class
A matrix \(A\) is diagonalizable if and only if, for each eigenvalue of \(A\), its algebraic multiplicity equals its geometric multiplicity.
If \(A\) has distinct eigenvalues, then \(A\) is diagonalizable. The converse need not be true.
An \(n\times n\) matrix is diagonalizable if and only if it has \(n\) linearly independent eigenvectors.
The matrix formed by taking the eigenvectors of \(A\) as columns, \(P=[X_1\ X_2\ X_3]\) for the \(3\times3\) case, is called the modal matrix of \(A\).
The diagonal matrix \(D\) is called the spectral matrix; its diagonal entries are the eigenvalues of \(A\).
The transformation \(P^{-1}AP=D\) is called a similarity transformation.
